summary: Build the public read-only lookup experience
description: Render the shared lookup result accessibly without introducing a browser-only truth path, and expose that exact surface through a thin Vercel deployment adapter.
acceptance: R-1: The interface leads with normalized number context, evidence, unknowns, confidence, and spoofing-safe wording.
R-2: Accessibility, responsive layout, privacy, and no-results states have automated or documented proof.
R-3: A Vercel deployment serves the website and canonical HTTP lookup through one same-origin public URL.

R-4: Public repository documentation accurately distinguishes the implemented read-only wedge, the historical v0.1.0 foundation release, the remaining mutation and operations backlog, and the authenticated production-hosting boundary.

review_history.evidence: Acceptance R-1/R-2/R-3 verified: one canonical HTTP path; evidence, unknowns, confidence and spoofing language lead the result; semantic, responsive, privacy, empty/error/success, live bundle, headers, API, and browser evidence all pass. Anonymous-preview expiry is documented and does not alter implementation correctness.

Public README, architecture, onboarding, and implementation-plan maturity copy still describes the implemented CLI/MCP/HTTP/web read-only wedge as future or unimplemented; public deployment work cannot be considered coherent until these claims match repository reality.

Rework approved: R-4 is now enforced by repository tests and public docs consistently describe the implemented read-only wedge, remaining safety backlog, and persistent-hosting boundary. R-1/R-2/R-3 evidence remains intact; all focused and repository gates pass.

Authenticated production verification found /healthz returns 404 on the stable Vercel alias because vercel.json rewrites only /v1/lookup. Homepage, lookup success, lookup validation, and security headers pass. Add a regression test and the minimal same-origin health rewrite before redeploying.
